evals.name: zero2-is-bandwidth-free
evals.prompt: 우리는 지금 DDP로 학습 중인데 메모리가 빠듯해. ZeRO-2로 바꾸면 통신량이 늘어나서 느려질까?
evals.expected_output: Says ZeRO-2 moves the same 2Ψ as DDP, justified by AllReduce = ReduceScatter ∘ AllGather, so it is effectively free; contrasts with ZeRO-3 at 3Ψ.

assertions.description: States ZeRO-2's volume as the literal quantity 2Ψ (twice the parameter count), not just 'about the same' or 'roughly equal'
Justifies it with the identity AllReduce = ReduceScatter ∘ AllGather, and notes ring all-reduce already executes it in those two phases
Gives ZeRO-3/FSDP's volume as the literal quantity 3Ψ, and attributes the extra Ψ to gathering parameters twice — once for forward, once for backward
Gives the per-rank model-state formula: DDP 2Ψ+2Ψ+KΨ = 16Ψ versus ZeRO-2's 2Ψ + (2Ψ+KΨ)/d, with K=12 for fp32-master Adam
Concludes there is no bandwidth argument for keeping DDP over ZeRO-2, rather than hedging that ZeRO-2 is 'probably fine'
Notes ZeRO shards model states but NOT activations, so it does not help if activations are what is tight

evals.name: pipeline-bubble-formula
evals.prompt: Why does pipeline parallelism have a bubble, and how large is it? How do I make it smaller?
evals.expected_output: Gives bubble = (p-1)/(m+p-1), explains fill/drain, says raise m, and notes m trades against d because B = b*m*d.

assertions.description: States the bubble fraction as (p−1)/(m+p−1) explicitly
Explains it as the pipeline fill and drain phases where stages have no micro-batch to run
Says the lever is increasing the number of micro-batches m relative to p
Notes that raising m at fixed global batch forces d down, because B = b·m·d — so PP and DP compete

evals.name: tp-must-stay-in-node
evals.prompt: I have 2 nodes with 8 H100s each. Should I set tensor parallel degree to 16 so the model shards across both nodes?
evals.expected_output: Says no; TP's per-layer 4*b*s*h all-reduce is on the critical path and must stay within the NVLink domain; suggests t<=8 and PP or ZeRO across nodes.

assertions.description: Advises against TP=16 spanning two nodes
Identifies TP's cost as roughly 4 all-reduces per layer per step on activations of size b·s·h
Notes this traffic is on the critical path between matmuls and cannot be overlapped/hidden, unlike DP's all-reduce
Gives the rule that t should not exceed the NVLink domain / node size, and suggests PP or ZeRO-3 for the inter-node axis

evals.name: sp-vs-cp-distinction
evals.prompt: sequence parallelism이랑 context parallelism이 같은 거야? 차이가 뭔지 정확히 알려줘.
evals.expected_output: Separates them: Megatron SP shards only LN/dropout regions and is volume-neutral; CP/ring attention shards the whole sequence including attention with K/V rotation and is its own mesh axis.

assertions.description: States clearly that they are NOT the same thing
Describes Megatron sequence parallelism as sharding only the layernorm/dropout (non-tensor-parallel) regions, leaving attention unchanged
Notes SP replaces TP's all-reduce with a reduce-scatter/all-gather pair at the same total volume, so it is essentially free memory
Describes context parallelism as sharding the full sequence with K/V blocks circulating in a ring, and as a separate mesh axis c

evals.name: mesh-design-with-invariants
evals.prompt: 1024 H100s, a 405B dense model, sequence length 8192, target global batch 2048 samples. Give me a concrete parallelism configuration.
evals.expected_output: Gives a full (d,t,p,c) tuple, shows d*t*p*c = 1024, keeps t<=8 in-node, shows B = b*m*d = 2048, and checks m >= 4p for the bubble.

assertions.description: Gives a complete (d, t, p, c) tuple
Explicitly evaluates d·t·p·c as arithmetic and shows it equals 1024
Names the batch invariant as B = b·m·d and shows the arithmetic reaching 2048, not merely deriving a gradient-accumulation count
Rejects at least one specific alternative by arithmetic — e.g. notes (8,16,8,1) also multiplies to 1024 but puts tensor parallelism across two nodes
Prices each axis in communication-volume terms (TP's 4·L·b·s·h on the critical path, PP's 2·b·s·h point-to-point per boundary, DP's 3Ψ under ZeRO-3)
Quantifies the pipeline bubble using (p−1)/(m+p−1), and gives the interleaved value (1/v)·(p−1)/m if interleaving is proposed
Identifies activations rather than model states as the binding constraint, e.g. by showing 16Ψ/1024 is trivially small

evals.name: moe-active-vs-total
evals.prompt: DeepSeek-V3는 671B total에 37B activated라던데, MFU 계산할 때랑 메모리 계산할 때 각각 어느 숫자를 써야 해?
evals.expected_output: MFU/FLOPs use N_active (37B) via 6N; memory planning uses N_total (671B) since every expert must be resident somewhere.

assertions.description: Says FLOPs and MFU must use the activated parameter count (37B), not the total
Says memory planning must use the total parameter count (671B), because all experts must live somewhere
Warns that using N_total for MFU inflates it (by roughly E/k, here about 18x)
